The '''2025 Toronto Blue Jays season''' was the [[2025 Major League Baseball season|49th season]] of the [[Toronto Blue Jays]] franchise, and the Blue Jays' 34th full season (36th overall) at [[Rogers Centre]]. The Blue Jays dramatically improved upon their last place record, 74-88, from last season with a first-place record of 94-68. The season was the third time the Blue Jays won the [[American League pennant]], advancing to the [[2025 World Series]] against the [[2024 World Series|defending champ]] [[2025 Los Angeles Dodgers season|Los Angeles Dodgers]], their third appearance in franchise history and first since [[1993 World Series|1993]]. The season ended with their first World Series loss in franchise history, falling to the Dodgers in seven games with Game 7 going into [[extra innings]] at home.

On August 22, the Blue Jays won their 75th game, guaranteeing a better total than their 74–88 record from [[2024 Toronto Blue Jays season|last year]] following a 5–2 victory over the [[2025 Miami Marlins season|Miami Marlins]].

On September 21, the Blue Jays clinched a return to the [[2025 Major League Baseball postseason|postseason]] after a one-year absence with an 8–5 win over the [[2025 Kansas City Royals season|Kansas City Royals]].<ref name="Blue Jays headed back to postseason with sights set on East crown">{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/blue-jays-clinch-postseason-berth-2025|title=Blue Jays headed back to postseason with sights set on East crown|last=Matheson|first=Keegan|work=MLB.com|date=September 21, 2025|accessdate=September 21, 2025}}</ref> On September 28, the Blue Jays won the [[American League East]] division for the first time since [[2015 Toronto Blue Jays season|2015]] by virtue of a head-to-head tiebreaker against the [[2025 New York Yankees season|New York Yankees]], 8–5, with a 13–4 victory against the [[2025 Tampa Bay Rays season|Tampa Bay Rays]] in their final regular season game, a first-round bye, and home-field advantage throughout the [[American League]] playoffs.<ref name="AL East belongs up north! Blue Jays clinch first division title since 2015">{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/news/blue-jays-win-2025-al-east-division-title|title= AL East belongs up north! Blue Jays clinch first division title since 2015|last=Matheson|first=Keegan|work=MLB.com|date=September 28, 2025|accessdate=September 29, 2025}}</ref> The team won the [[2025 American League Division Series|Division Series]] with [[home-field advantage]] against the fourth seed New York Yankees, victors of the [[2025 American League Wild Card Series|Wild Card Series]] over [[Red Sox–Yankees rivalry|archrival]] [[2025 Boston Red Sox season|Boston Red Sox]], earning the team their first [[American League Championship Series]] appearance since [[2016 Toronto Blue Jays season|2016]]. On October 20, the Blue Jays defeated the [[2025 Seattle Mariners season|Seattle Mariners]] at home in seven games in the [[2025 American League Championship Series|2025 ALCS]] to advance to the 2025 World Series. In that series, they faced the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers, which the Blue Jays lost in seven games.

After the season, [[Buck Martinez]], Blue Jays' color analyst since [[1987 Toronto Blue Jays season|1987]], announced his retirement.<ref name="star25">{{cite news |last1=Ngabo|first1=Gilbert|title=Buck Martinez returns to Blue Jays broadcasts after stepping away for cancer treatment. He thinks this team could go all the way|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/blue-jays/buck-martinez-returns-to-blue-jays-broadcasts-after-stepping-away-for-cancer-treatment-he-thinks/article_8a72c8c6-cec1-4141-8d12-177bad8e0adf.html|work=Toronto Star|date=8 August 2025}}</ref>

The Toronto Blue Jays drew an average home attendance of 35,184, the 9th-highest of all MLB teams.<ref>https://www.espn.com/mlb/attendance/_/year/2025</ref>

==Offseason==

The Blue Jays offseason began with [[Ryan Yarbrough]] and [[Génesis Cabrera]] electing [[Free agency (Major League Baseball)|free agency]].<ref>{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions October 2024|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2024/10|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref><ref name="NovTransactions">{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions November 2024|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2024/11|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> [[Braydon Fisher]] was signed on a minor league deal on November 18.<ref name="NovTransactions"/> On November 22, they non-tendered former All-Star closer [[Jordan Romano]], after he posted a 6.59 ERA in 2024 while dealing with elbow issues, avoiding a projected $7.75 million salary. They also non-tendered [[Dillon Tate]].<ref>{{citeweb|title=Romano non-tendered by Toronto, becomes a free agent|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jordan-romano-non-tendered-by-blue-jays|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> On December 3rd, the Blue Jays signed Michael Stefanic to a minor league contract.<ref name="DecTransactions">{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions December 2024|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2024/12|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

The first major move of the offseason came on December 10, when the Blue Jays traded [[Spencer Horwitz]] and minor league outfielder Nick Mitchell to the [[Cleveland Guardians]] for former All-Star and 3x [[Gold Glove]] winner [[Andrés Giménez]], and reliever [[Nick Sandlin]]. The Guardians traded Gimenez after underwhelming offensive performance, and to get rid of his 7-year $106.5 million contract extension signed in 2023. Later that same day, the Guardians would go on to trade Horwitz to the [[Pittsburgh Pirates]] for [[Luis Ortiz (pitcher, born 1999)|Luis Ortiz]], [[Michael Kennedy (baseball)|Michael Kennedy]] and [[Josh Hartle]].<ref>{{citeweb|title=Guardians trade Giménez in three-team swap with Jays, Bucs|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/guardians-trade-andres-gimenez-to-blue-jays-for-spencer-horwitz|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

On December 11, the Blue Jays selected [[Angel Bastardo]] in the [[Rule 5 Draft]] from the [[Boston Red Sox]]. Bastardo spent the entire 2025 season on the [[injured list]] recovering from [[Tommy John surgery]].<ref>{{citeweb|title=Blue Jays select Bastardo|url=https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-blue-jays-select-bastardo-in-2025-rule-5-draft|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> The Blue Jays signed their first major league free agent on December 13, bringing back relief pitcher [[Yimi García]] on a 2-year, $15 million contract. They had previously traded him at the 2024 trade deadline to the [[Seattle Mariners]] for [[Jonatan Clase]] and catcher Jacob Sharp. <ref>{{citeweb|title=Blue Jays bringing back Yimi García on 2-year deal|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/yimi-garcia-blue-jays-contract|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> On December 20, the Blue Jays signed [[Josh Walker (baseball)|Josh Walker]] to a major league deal, and signed [[Eric Lauer]] and [[Ali Sánchez]] to minor league contracts.

The Blue Jays were also rumoured to be among the finalists for top free agents [[Juan Soto]] and [[Corbin Burnes]], offering around $700 million for Soto<ref>{{citeweb|title=How far Blue Jays went in pursuit of Juan Soto|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mlb/article/how-far-blue-jays-went-in-pursuit-of-juan-soto/|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> and offering more to Burnes than the [[Arizona Diamondbacks]], who ended up signing him, did.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Blue Jays running out of long-term rotation options after missing out on Burnes|url=https://www.tsn.ca/mlb/toronto-blue-jays-running-out-of-long-term-rotation-options-after-missing-out-on-corbin-burnes-1.2226302|website=TSN.ca|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

On January 10, the Blue Jays signed all-star closer [[Jeff Hoffman]] to a 3-year $33 million contract. There were rumours of Hoffman attempting to become a starter, however Jays GM [[Ross Atkins (baseball)|Ross Atkins]] confirmed Hoffman was signed as a reliever. This move came a day after Jordan Romano signed with the [[Philadelphia Phillies]], essentially completing a closer swap between the two teams. The Jays originally drafted Hoffman in the first round of the [[2014 Major League Baseball draft]] before trading him for [[Troy Tulowitzki]] in 2015.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Blue Jays ink RHP Hoffman to 3-year deal|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jeff-hoffman-contract-with-blue-jays|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

On January 15, the Blue Jays traded Brett de Geus to the Pirates for cash considerations.<ref name="JanTransactions">{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions January 2025|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2025/1|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> On January 17th, with the Jays looking to sign top international free agent [[Roki Sasaki]], they traded a [[player to be named later]] to the Guardians for [[Myles Straw]], international bonus pool money, and cash. Similar to Gimenez, Straw provided elite defense, but underperformed offensively and had an unsavoury contract, owed $13.8 million over the last two years of the contract.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Guardians send Straw to Blue Jays for player to be named or cash|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/myles-straw-traded-to-blue-jays-from-guardians|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> After missing out on Sasaki, the Jays signed 17 international free agents on January 18, most notably shortstops Christopher Polanco and Juan Sanchez.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Toronto adds star D.R. shortstop in '25 international class|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/blue-jays-2025-international-prospect-signings|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

On January 20, the Blue Jays signed outfielder [[Anthony Santander]] to a 5-year, $92.5 million contract. Coming off a 44-[[home run]] season with the [[Baltimore Orioles]], Santander was one of the premier free agents available, and was expected to be a weapon batting behind star first baseman [[Vladimir Guerrero Jr.]].<ref>{{citeweb|title=Santander embraces 'new brothers,' old connections in Toronto|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/anthony-santander-joins-blue-jays|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> On January 22, the Jays signed [[Dicky Lovelady]] to a minor league contract.<ref name="JanTransactions"/>

On February 4, the Jays signed legendary pitcher [[Max Scherzer]] to a one-year, $15.5 million deal. At the time, Scherzer was an 8-time all-star, 3-time [[Cy Young]] winner, and 2-time World Series champion.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Blue Jays finalize 1-year, $15.5M deal with 3-time Cy winner Scherzer|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/max-scherzer-blue-jays-contract|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> Scherzer was expected to play an important role beyond the mound, including mentoring younger pitchers such as [[Trey Yesavage]]. On February 17, the Blue Jays signed [[Jacob Barnes]] to a minor league deal. On February 21, they brought Ryan Yarbrough back on a minor league deal.<ref>{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions February 2025|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2025/2|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref> They would also bring back Dillon Tate on a major league contract on March 12. <ref>{{citeweb|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions March 2025|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2025/3|website=MLB.com|access-date=2026-01-08}}</ref>

===March and April===
The Blue Jays began the 2025 season at home against the [[2025 Baltimore Orioles season|Baltimore Orioles]], splitting a four-game series with one of their [[American League East|AL East]] rivals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coastreporter.net/ontario-news/springer-bassitt-help-blue-jays-split-season-opening-series-with-orioles-10450682|title=Springer, Bassitt help Blue Jays split season-opening series with Orioles|last=Wharnsby|first=Tim|work=coastreporter.net|date=March 30, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref> Offseason acquisition [[Max Scherzer]] was injured in his start on March 29, and was placed on the injured list.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/max-scherzer-to-injured-list-with-right-thumb-inflammation|title=Scherzer heads to IL with right thumb injury|last=Matheson|first=Keegan|work=MLB.com|date=March 30, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref> The [[2025 Washington Nationals season|Washington Nationals]] were [[Sweep (sports)|swept]] by the Jays in the next series, with [[Easton Lucas]] taking Scherzer's rotation spot and pitching five scoreless innings in the finale.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mlb/article/lucas-steps-into-void-to-help-blue-jays-sweep-nationals/|title=Lucas steps into void to help Blue Jays sweep Nationals|last=Davidi|first=Shi|work=[[Sportsnet]]|date=April 2, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref> Traveling to Queens for their first road trip of 2025, the Blue Jays were swept by the [[2025 New York Mets season|New York Mets]] over a three-game series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mlb/article/francis-keeps-rolling-but-blue-jays-offence-falls-short-in-mets-sweep/|title=Francis keeps rolling, but Blue Jays offence falls short in Mets sweep|last=Davidi|first=Shi|work=[[Sportsnet]]|date=April 6, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref>

On April 7, the Blue Jays signed Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to a 14-year, $500 million contract extension. The extension is the largest contract in franchise history, eclipsing the six-year, $150 million contract issued to [[George Springer]], and is [[List of largest sports contracts|the second-largest contract in MLB history]] in present-day value and the highest for a one-team professional athlete in any team sport.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/baseball/mlb/blue-jays-announce-contract-vladimir-guerrero-jr-1.7505996|title=Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Officially Signs Extension|work=CBC.ca|accessdate=April 13, 2025}}</ref> Heading to Boston, Toronto nearly swept the [[2025 Boston Red Sox season|Boston Red Sox]] before falling in extra innings in the final game of the series. After the game, manager [[John Schneider (baseball)|John Schneider]] criticized home plate umpire [[Manny Gonzalez (umpire)|Manny Gonzalez]], saying "It's tough to battle nine hitters and an umpire... I've got all the respect in the world for them, but it wasn't a great day for him behind the plate."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/mlb/toronto-blue-jays-manager-john-schneider-rips-umpires-after-close-loss-to-boston-red-sox-1.2286762|title=Blue Jays manager Schneider rips umpires after close loss to Red Sox|work=TSN.ca|date=April 10, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref> To close their road trip, the Blue Jays went to Baltimore. The first game of the series was rained out (and was made up as a doubleheader in late July), and the teams split the other two games of the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/news/jeff-hoffman-secures-win-in-series-finale-vs-orioles|title=Hoffman lets loose after two-inning extras shutdown vs. O's: 'I love it'|last=Leckie|first=Paige|work=MLB.com|date=April 13, 2025|accessdate=April 14, 2025}}</ref>

===June===
[[File:Gimenez homers in stlouis 2025.png|thumb|[[Alejandro Kirk|Kirk]] and [[Bo Bichette|Bichette]] score on a three-run homer by [[Andrés Giménez|Giménez]] in St. Louis.]]
The Blue Jays began June by concluding a four-game sweep of the [[2025 Athletics season|Athletics]] at home.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Zicarelli |first1=Frank |title=Addison Barger's three-run bash lifts Blue Jays to series sweep of Athletics |url=https://torontosun.com/sports/baseball/toronto-blue-jays/bargers-three-run-bash-lifts-blue-jays-to-series-sweep-of-athletics |work=Toronto Sun |date=June 1, 2025}}</ref> They followed that by winning two of three from the [[2025 Philadelphia Phillies season|Philadelphia Phillies]] at home.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Delaney |first1=Ryley |title=Blue Jays series recap: Jays best Phillies in three-game series |url=https://www.msn.com/en-ca/sports/mlb/blue-jays-series-recap-jays-best-phillies-in-three-game-series/ |work=MSN |date=June 5, 2025}}</ref> Next, they won two of three against the [[2025 Minnesota Twins season|Minnesota Twins]] at [[Target Field]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lee and Vázquez go back to back to power Twins past Blue Jays 6-3 and avoid series sweep |url=https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/gametracker/recap/MLB_20250608_TOR@MIN/ |work=CBS Sports |agency=Associated Press |date=June 8, 2025}}</ref> The Blue Jays followed that up by sweeping the [[2025 St. Louis Cardinals season|St. Louis Cardinals]] in a three-game set on the road, resulting in their 12th win in 14 games and brought their record to 38–30.<ref>{{cite web |title=Blue Jays respond to every challenge in sweep of Cardinals |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mlb/article/blue-jays-responding-to-every-challenge-in-sweep-of-cardinals/ |website=sportsnet.ca |date=June 12, 2025}}</ref>

===July===
From June 30 to July 3, the Blue Jays won all four games against the [[2025 New York Yankees season|New York Yankees]] at home and by doing so, overtook them for first place in the AL East.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Matheson |first1=Keegan |title=4-game sweep of Yanks finds Blue Jays alone in 1st this late for first time since '16 |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/blue-jays-alone-in-first-place-after-4-game-sweep-of-yankees |website=mlb.com |date=July 4, 2025}}</ref> On July 21, the Blue Jays set a franchise record by winning their 11th straight game at home, beating the Yankees in the first game of another three-game set against them.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Davidi |first1=Shi |title=Blue Jays do all the little things in win over Yankees to cap record home streak |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mlb/article/blue-jays-do-all-the-little-things-in-win-over-yankees-to-cap-record-home-streak/ |website=sportsnet.ca |date=July 22, 2025}}</ref>

The Blue Jays then traded for relief pitcher [[Seranthony Domínguez]] from the Baltimore Orioles, starting pitcher [[Shane Bieber]] from the Cleveland Guardians, and [[Louis Varland]] and [[Ty France]] from the Minnesota Twins before the trade deadline. The Blue Jays traded away [[Will Wagner (baseball)|Will Wagner]].

===August===
On August 6, the Blue Jays set another franchise record and the MLB record by recording 63 hits in a three-game series against the [[2025 Colorado Rockies season|Colorado Rockies]] in [[Coors Field]] and also established a franchise mark with 45 runs in the three-game set.<ref>{{cite news |title=Guerrero and Blue Jays rout Rockies 20-1 to cap Coors Field barrage |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/recap/_/gameId/401696629 |agency=Associated Press |date=August 6, 2025}}</ref>

===September===
The Blue Jays clinched the postseason on September 21 after beating the [[2025 Kansas City Royals season|Kansas City Royals]] in [[Kauffman Stadium]].<ref name="Blue Jays headed back to postseason with sights set on East crown" /> The Blue Jays continued their poor run of form in late September allowing the [[2025 New York Yankees season|New York Yankees]] to tie the Blue Jays' win total, with the Blue Jays remaining the division leader due to the season series tiebreaker as the Blue Jays have a head-to-head record of 8–5 over the Yankees. Following a subsequent sweep of the [[2025 Tampa Bay Rays season|Tampa Bay Rays]], the Blue Jays clinched the Division Title in front of a home crowd on the last game of the regular season, despite having a tied overall record with the Yankees.<ref name="AL East belongs up north! Blue Jays clinch first division title since 2015" />

==Transactions==
===March===
* On March 27, designated Tommy Nance, Zach Pop, and Nick Robertson for assignment, placed Daulton Varsho on the 10-day injured list, placed Ryan Burr and Erik Swanson on the 15-day injured list, and selected the contracts of Jacob Barnes, Alan Roden, and Myles Straw.<ref name="March Transactions">{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2025/03|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions in March|work=MLB.com|accessdate=April 3, 2025}}</ref>
* On March 29, outrighted Tommy Nance to Triple-A Buffalo.<ref name="March Transactions"/>
* On March 30, placed Max Scherzer on the 15-day injured list, designated Richard Lovelady for assignment, recalled Easton Lucas, and selected the contract of Mason Fluharty.<ref name="March Transactions"/>

===April===
* On April 1, traded Nick Robertson to the Houston Astros for Edinson Batista.<ref name="April Transactions">{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/roster/transactions/2025/04|title=Toronto Blue Jays Transactions in April|work=MLB.com|accessdate=April 3, 2025}}</ref>
* On April 2, released Zach Pop.<ref name="April Transactions"/>
* On April 3, outrighted Richard Lovelady to Triple-A Buffalo.<ref name="April Transactions"/>
* On April 15, placed Nathan Lukes on the paternity list and recalled Addison Barger.<ref name="April Transactions"/>
* On April 17, optioned Davis Schneider to the Triple-A Buffalo Bisons.<ref name="April Transactions"/>
* On April 18, activated Nathan Lukes.<ref name="April Transactions"/>
